features.name: Close the version-drift/silent-fallback gap in feat-007's .venv preference logic (multi-model review)
features.description: Reviewed feat-007's fallback pattern with codex-kiro (failed once with a hard stream error, succeeded on retry) and agy (a third, genuinely different model family -- brought in specifically because codex-kiro had just failed once). codex-kiro found a real gap: '[[ -x "$MYPY" ]] || MYPY="mypy"' only proves executability, not that the venv is the right Python version -- a stale/rebuilt .venv would silently be used with zero warning. Fixed in types-guard.sh and run-tests.sh: both now compare .venv's actual python3 --version against .python-version and fail loud (exit 2 for the Stop-hook gate, exit 1 for the CLI) on any mismatch or broken binary, instead of silently falling back to ambient tooling. Confirmed by actually simulating drift (echo 9.9.9 > .python-version) and watching it block, not just reading the code. agy required --dangerously-skip-permissions to run at all in headless mode; its review then produced two confident but FALSE claims (Python 3.14.7 'does not exist' -- installed and used all session; httpx2/httpcore2 are 'potential typosquats' -- both real PyPI packages, a legit anthropic transitive dep per pip show/pipdeptree) which were checked and refuted, not accepted. One claim converged across both models and checked out against PyPI directly: google-generativeai is genuinely deprecated (legacy, support ended 2025-11-30, successor google-genai) -- flagged as a real, confirmed, NOT-yet-actioned finding since migrating it touches shipped code (polish_engine.py), a different-shaped change than this session's scope.
features.evidence: Simulated version drift (`echo 9.9.9 > .python-version`) -> `bash .claude/hooks/types-guard.sh` exits 2 with rebuild instructions, `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` exits 1 with the same, both correctly refusing to silently fall back; restored the pin, reran clean. `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` -> 53 passed, 0 failed after the fix. `pip show httpx2`/`pipdeptree --reverse -p httpx2` confirmed agy's typosquat claim false. WebFetch on pypi.org/project/google-generativeai/ confirmed the deprecation claim true. google-generativeai -> google-genai migration explicitly NOT done -- open finding for a future session, recorded in docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/summary.md and progress-detail.md Part 8.

features.name: Lecture 2: controlled variable exclusion test, attempt 2 (non-null result)
features.description: Attempt 1 (mirror a 20-line sibling file, strip Instructions/State/Feedback across 4 fresh general-purpose subagents) came back null -- all 4 conditions succeeded identically because the task was fully answerable from the sibling file alone. Attempt 2 used a harder task (add a whole new shellcheck verification gate across 4 real integration points: guard script, harness-verify.sh wiring, two hook arrays, a test file) against the same baseline-plus-3-ablations method (one git-archive baseline, 3 variants each missing exactly one of AGENTS.md/state files/test-running capability, never built independently). Result: non-null. All 4 conditions completed the core task, but only the condition with AGENTS.md present (baseline) went from finding a genuine pre-existing shellcheck bug (test_install_agents_md.sh:210, SC1087) to fixing it; the two conditions without AGENTS.md (no-instructions, no-state) found the identical bug independently in separate sandboxes and explicitly flagged it as out of scope instead of fixing it. The fourth condition (no-feedback) had a confound caught after all 4 results were in: its ablation deleted scripts/tests/ wholesale to remove the Feedback subsystem, which happened to delete the exact file the bug lived in -- so its silence on the bug is a byproduct of the ablation, not a finding, and it was excluded from this specific comparison. The correlation (AGENTS.md present -> fixed rather than flagged) is real and cross-validated (3 independent sandboxes found the identical bug on their own), but AGENTS.md contains no instruction resembling 'fix incidental bugs you find' (grepped directly, no match) -- so the causal mechanism is explicitly recorded as unconfirmed, not overclaimed as proven.
features.evidence: 4 fresh general-purpose subagents dispatched concurrently, one per variant directory under /tmp/exclusion-test-v2/ (baseline/no-instructions/no-state/no-feedback), each given only its directory and the task text, no mention of the experiment. Read .claude/settings.json directly in each variant afterward -- confirmed the new hook entry landed in both Stop and SubagentStop arrays in all 4 with the same shape as sibling entries. Read (not just re-ran) the no-feedback and no-state test files to resolve two apparent discrepancies (a scenario/assertion-count mismatch, a harness scanner false-positive flag on settings.json) -- both confirmed as false alarms by reading the full file content. Checked all 4 variants' new guard scripts for bash-4+-only constructs (mapfile, declare -A) against AGENTS.md's documented bash-3.2 floor -- none used them, including the 3 conditions that never saw that constraint stated anywhere (a mechanically-checked negative result). Confirmed the no-feedback confound directly via `ls` for the buggy file's existence in that checkout, rather than accepting the 'not applicable' cell at face value. Full method and results: docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/progress-detail.md Part 9.

features.name: Lecture 2: affordance analysis (Gulf of Execution / Gulf of Evaluation) -- Lecture 2 now fully closed
features.description: Classified two real cases from this training session into Norman's two gulfs, no synthetic cases needed. Case 1 (polish-input hook repeatedly fabricating fake refusals/identities instead of a genuine paraphrase, across this same session) is Gulf of Evaluation: the hook has no feedback loop on its own output (no schema/shape/confidence check before injecting the polish model's response as context), so distinguishing genuine paraphrase from hallucinated tangent fell entirely on ad hoc content-level judgment, redone from scratch each occurrence. Case 2 (all 4 feat-009 exclusion-test subagents independently hitting the same spurious exit-128 types-guard.sh failure in their git-archive'd sandboxes with no .git directory) is Gulf of Execution: the feedback itself was clear (an unambiguous git error), but harness-verify.sh offers only one action -- run all 8 gates -- with no way to express 'run just the gate relevant to my change,' so every agent paid the same diagnostic cost independently. Neither gap was fixed as part of this exercise -- it is a classification exercise, not a remediation task. This closes out Lecture 2's last open item: both subsystems (Tools, Environment) and both exercises (exclusion test, affordance analysis) are now done.
features.evidence: Both cases drawn from this session's own real events (the polish-input hook malfunctions and the feat-009 exit-128 failures), not invented. Full classification writeup: docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/progress-detail.md Part 10, docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/summary.md.

features.name: Migrate polish-input Gemini backend from google-generativeai to google-genai (API key only)
features.description: google-generativeai is deprecated (flagged in feat-008). Live check before migrating: this machine's only Gemini credential was the Antigravity OAuth session, and it already failed with 403 ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT under the old SDK. google-genai cannot use OAuth for the Gemini API at all: Client() raises 'No API key was provided' without a key, and bearer tokens are attached only in Vertex mode (_api_client.py:1463). Per user decision, ported _polish_gemini to genai.Client(api_key=...).models.generate_content with timeout in ms (the old SDK took seconds), removed GeminiAntigravityProvider and _read_antigravity_keychain_value, and log one hint (set GEMINI_API_KEY) when a Gemini provider had no key and nothing else succeeded. Default model changed from gemini-1.5-flash (no longer listed by Google, checked at ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models) to gemini-3.5-flash-lite. requirements-dev.txt regenerated from a clean venv (51 -> 43 packages; gRPC/protobuf gone); pyproject, _lib.sh pip package, README updated.
features.evidence: New tests failed first (2/3), then polish-input 40 passed. mypy clean; gitleaks + osv-scanner clean on the new manifest; harness-verify 9/9; run-tests --fast 56 passed. NOT verified live: no Gemini API key on this machine. Pre-existing installer gap: Homebrew python3 refuses global pip (PEP 668), so _lib.sh's pip step for polish-input fails here; ambient python still has only the old SDK. Not forced with --break-system-packages.
